title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and auto-labeling policies for non-Microsoft connected apps
summary: The briefing passes: its rollout dates, licensing statements, policy limitations and governance routes are supported. It correctly distinguishes the later Message Center rollout from the roadmap target and flags Microsoft's conflicting migration sequencing instructions.

claims.claim: Roadmap item 568075 concerns Microsoft Purview DLP and Information Protection auto-labeling for non-Microsoft connected apps.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention and Information Protection Auto-labeling capabilities now extend to non-Microsoft connected apps

claims.quote: Open Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy. [...] On the Locations page, toggle the Instances location to on. [...] select Edit > Specific instances > + Include instances

claims.claim: Security & Compliance PowerShell supports New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <policy name> -ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation All for all connected non-Microsoft apps in the retiring model.
claims.quote: The ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation parameter specifies the non-Microsoft cloud apps to include in the DLP policy. You can use the value All to include all connected apps.

claims.claim: The ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation parameter requires Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator membership.
claims.quote: This parameter requires membership in the Compliance Administrator or Compliance Data Administrator roles in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: The ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation reference points to the retiring Instances implementation rather than establishing applicability to dedicated app locations.
claims.quote: For more information about DLP for non-Microsoft cloud apps, see Use data loss prevention policies for non-Microsoft cloud apps.

claims.claim: App connector setup has app-specific guides and authentication steps.
claims.quote: Follow the instructions in the corresponding app-specific API connector guide. These instructions include the required permissions and authentication steps.

claims.claim: Creating the equivalent Purview policies does not remove the original Defender for Cloud Apps file policies.
claims.quote: Does migrating remove my original file policies? No. Migration creates new equivalent policies in Purview.

claims.claim: Activity explorer supports monitoring DLP activity for these non-Microsoft apps.
claims.quote: Activity explorer supports non-Microsoft connected app policies. You can monitor DLP policy activity for your non-Microsoft apps in the same way you monitor Microsoft 365 locations.

claims.claim: Activity explorer also supports monitoring labeling activity for these non-Microsoft apps.
claims.quote: Activity explorer supports non-Microsoft connected app policies. You can monitor labeling policy activity for your non-Microsoft apps in the same way you monitor Microsoft 365 locations.

claims.claim: DLP alerts are supported for these connected app policies.
claims.quote: DLP alerts are supported for non-Microsoft connected app policies. Alerts appear in the DLP alerts dashboard alongside alerts from other locations.

claims.claim: The reviewed sources do not say this new capability changes existing behaviour for tenants that create no policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "non-Microsoft connected" "PowerShell" "locations" DLP auto-labeling. Read roadmap, MC1449180, both feature pages and migration guidance: no automatic new-policy enforcement stated; the separate file-policy retirement is documented and reported.
